prompt.context: Your client is a U.S. state's social services agency. The agency is responsible for administering the state's social work programs. Recently, the state legislature passed a law that will change the agency's funding structure. Previously, the agency had been funded at a fixed dollar amount. Now, under the new law, the agency will be paid according to performance, as measured by the number of interviews they conduct with state social work clients.
prompt.question: The agency has hired you to determine how the change will affect them and what they should do about it.

clarifying_info.q: What activities does the agency perform?
clarifying_info.a: For the purpose of simplicity, the agency's only activity is conducting interviews.

clarifying_info.q: How was the agency previously funded?
clarifying_info.a: Previously, the agency received $50,000 per employee per year.

clarifying_info.q: How much of that cost went to salary and how much to overhead and other costs?
clarifying_info.a: On average $30,000 went to salary and $20,000 went to overhead.

clarifying_info.q: How many employees does the agency have?
clarifying_info.a: Unknown. This case is on a per-employee basis.

clarifying_info.q: How will the agency be funded after the change?
clarifying_info.a: The agency will be paid $25 per interview.

clarifying_info.q: How many interviews does each state social worker conduct per day?
clarifying_info.a: Currently each social worker conducts an average of 5 interviews per day.

framework: Understand previous funding structure: fixed $50,000 per employee per year ($30K salary + $20K overhead)
Understand new funding structure: $25 per interview conducted
Calculate revenue under new system (at current interview rate) and compare to previous funding
Identify the budget shortfall and quantify it
Explore revenue-side levers to close the gap (increase number of interviews)
Explore cost-side levers to close the gap (reduce overhead and salary costs)

questions.prompt: Calculate the agency's annual revenue per employee under the new funding structure, assuming no operational changes, and identify the budget shortfall.
questions.guidance: Candidate should calculate: 250 workdays/year × 5 interviews/day × $25/interview = $31,250 per employee per year. Compare to previous $50,000: shortfall = $50,000 - $31,250 = $18,750 per employee per year.

questions.prompt: What happens to revenue if the agency boosts interviews from 5 to 6 per social worker per day?
questions.guidance: Under the current system, the agency can boost daily interviews from 5 to 6. Candidate should recalculate revenue and remaining shortfall.

math.answer: Remaining shortfall: $12,500 per employee per year

questions.prompt: How long does each interview take, and is there a way to use process improvements to further increase the number of interviews per day?
questions.guidance: Candidate should ask about interview duration. Each interview takes 1 hour: 40 mins for the interview and 20 mins for follow-up data entry. A transcription software can cut data entry from 20 to 10 minutes. The 10 minutes saved per interview × 6 interviews = 60 minutes freed per day, enabling 1 additional interview per day (7 total).

math.setup: Time saved per day with transcription software, then new annual revenue
steps: 10 min saved × 6 interviews/day = 60 min saved/day = 1 additional interview/day
Remaining shortfall = $50,000 - $43,750 = $6,250 per employee per year
math.answer: Remaining shortfall: $6,250 per employee per year after implementing transcription software

questions.prompt: Are there alternative or supplemental funding sources the agency could pursue?
questions.guidance: Candidate should explore charitable or grant funding. The agency can obtain $1,000 per employee per year from a private charitable trust. Remaining shortfall: $6,250 - $1,000 = $5,250 per employee per year.

steps: $6,250 - $1,000 = $5,250 remaining shortfall per employee per year
math.answer: Remaining shortfall: $5,250 per employee per year

questions.prompt: What cost-cutting options exist, particularly on the overhead side?
questions.guidance: Candidate should explore overhead reduction. Consolidating offices into other state agency buildings saves $4,000 per employee per year. Remaining shortfall: $5,250 - $4,000 = $1,250 per employee per year.

steps: $5,250 - $4,000 = $1,250 remaining shortfall per employee per year
math.answer: Remaining shortfall: $1,250 per employee per year

questions.prompt: Are all social workers paid the same salary? If not, can the agency restructure its staffing costs?
questions.guidance: Salary distribution: 30% paid $25K/year, 40% paid $30K/year, 30% paid $35K/year. The agency can convert half of the highest-paid workers (30%) to the lowest pay grade. New distribution: 45% at $25K, 40% at $30K, 15% at $35K. Savings = 15% × ($35K - $25K) = $1,500 per employee per year. This actually closes the $1,250 gap and produces $250 surplus per employee per year.

math.setup: Salary restructuring: convert half of the 30% at $35K to $25K pay grade
steps: Half of 30% = 15% of employees moved from $35K to $25K
Net position: $1,500 savings - $1,250 shortfall = $250 surplus per employee per year
math.answer: $1,500 savings per employee per year; results in $250 surplus, fully closing the gap

recommendation: The funding change to performance-based pay at $25 per interview creates an $18,750 per employee per year budget shortfall if the agency continues operating as-is.
By implementing a combination of revenue increases and cost reductions, the agency can fully close the gap and achieve a small surplus of $250 per employee per year.

Revenue increases: boost daily interviews from 5 to 6 (+$6,250), implement transcription software to reach 7 interviews/day (+$6,250), and pursue charitable trust funding (+$1,000) — total revenue gain of $13,500.
Cost reductions: consolidate offices with other state agencies (-$4,000 overhead) and restructure salary grades (-$1,500) — total cost savings of $5,500.
Combined impact: $13,500 revenue gain + $5,500 cost savings = $19,000 improvement vs. $18,750 gap, yielding a $250 surplus per employee per year.
risks: Increasing interview volume may reduce interview quality and harm service delivery outcomes.
The transcription software introduces IT implementation risk and ongoing maintenance costs.
Office consolidation may reduce operational flexibility and harm employee morale.
Charitable trust funding is not guaranteed to be sustainable year-over-year.
Salary restructuring may increase turnover among higher-paid experienced workers.
next_steps: Evaluate the cost of the transcription software to confirm it is covered by the $250 surplus.
Develop a change management plan for office consolidation and salary restructuring.
Pursue and formalize the charitable trust funding agreement.
Monitor interview quality metrics after increasing daily volume to ensure service standards are maintained.
